Maria K.: quick decision needed — dedicated pools are starting to hit burst credit limits. Product wants graceful degradation for public API customers. Do we standardize on 429 precheck, 503 when runtime queues are full, or try a soft-slowdown header + 200s?
Devin: my vote: 429 for per-key/quota overage, 503 for infra/capacity problems. Keeps semantics clear.
Ash: fwiw clients usually implement backoff on 429 with Retry-After. We could add a `X-Redwood-Slowdown: 200ms` header to indicate we will buffer for N ms before rejecting. That could avoid full failover.
Jules: hmm. I worry about 429 semantics — many clients treat 429 as permanent throttling and stop retrying for longer. Also 503 is considered a transient server error so libs retry more aggressively -> could cause thundering herd.
Samir: we should separate reasons in telemetry: `shed_reason={quota|capacity|routing}`. If we return 503 for capacity, we attach `x-redwood-shed: capacity;queue-depth=73`. That lets us build console charts.
sre-bot: ALERT Triggered: dedicated-pool-us-east-3 burst_credit_exhausted count=14 window=5m
Maria K.: console/UX ask: Product wants per-key burst credits visible with a small timeline + suggested mitigation (reduce batch size, quantize, use dedicated). Also an option to opt into soft-queueing for paid tiers.
Devin: opt-in makes sense. Implementation concern: soft-queueing requires keeping KV caches alive while requests wait — increases memory pressure. Might be ok behind dedicated flows.
Ash: dev proposal snippet for router config: 
```
route: /v1/generate
precheck: true
precheck_response: 429
soft_queue:
  enabled: true
  max_hold_ms: 200
  fallback: 429
```
This would return `Retry-After` on 429 and `X-Redwood-Slowdown` when we hold.
Jules: I'd prefer a single canonical header to avoid client chaos, e.g. `X-Redwood-Shed: reason=quota;hold=120ms;remaining=12`. And document it in the SDKs.
Samir: telemetry hooks: please emit `shed_reason` + `hold_ms` + `pool_id` tags. Also add a derived metric: `ratio_of_shed_to_total_requests` per-org and per-key. That will help ops and product decide threshold tweaks.
Maria K.: rollout plan suggestion: 1) Start with 429 + Retry-After + internal `X-Redwood-Shed` (no docs) for 2 weeks in staging+canary. 2) Capture telemetry and create dashboard panels (per-key burst credits, p95 latency pre/post-shed, error budgets). 3) A/B test soft-queueing for 10% of traffic for paid tiers.
Devin: agree. For the dashboard add alert: `if ratio_of_shed_to_total_requests > 0.05 for 15m` -> paging for infra.
Ash: one more: small header footprint so mobile thin clients aren't broken. Keep header set to 2-3 keys. Also log full details to tracing only (not in response headers).
Jules: docs/SDK update: show recommended client backoff: exponential with jitter, respect `Retry-After` and `X-Redwood-Shed.hold`. We'll need sample code for Python/JS.
Samir: i'll add telemetry tags in the router PR. Also will emit a `shed_event` span.
Maria K.: OK next steps assigned: Devin + Ash implement the 429+slowdown headers router change (PR by EOD Thurs), Samir adds telemetry, Jules drafts SDK guidance, I'll create console wire for per-key burst credits. We'll reconvene after canary metrics. :thumbsup:
Devin: noted. I'll add a feature flag `edge.soft_shed_v1` so we can flip quickly.
Ash: PR will include the small `X-Redwood-Shed` schema and the router config.
Jules: will start docs draft.
sre-bot: NOTE: Created incident ticket #INC-4728 for burst_credit_exhaustion. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-4728
Maria K.: thanks all — landing on 429 + slowdown header for now, with telemetry to validate. If metrics show spike in client retries, we revisit to 503-based policy.
